story: Alex stared at the final notice on the kitchen table, the red ink bleeding into the cheap wood. He checked his bank balance for the tenth time in an hour, watching the single digit remain stubbornly unchanged while the silence of the empty apartment pressed against his eardrums. His fingers trembled as he scrolled through old contacts, sending messages to people he had not spoken to in a decade, begging for any small favor. He paced the narrow hallway until his breath came in shallow, jagged gasps and his chest tightened like a closing fist. He simply leaned against the wall and slid slowly to the floor.

Alex stared at the final notice on the kitchen table, the red ink bleeding into the cheap wood. He clawed at his own scalp, pulling hard enough to draw blood while his breath came in shallow, jagged hitches. Every drawer in the house had been emptied and shaken, yet the missing rent money remained a ghost. He sank to the linoleum floor, pressing his forehead against the cold surface until a dull ache pulsed behind his eyes. With trembling fingers, he began to dial a number he had promised himself he would never call again.

Alex stared at the final eviction notice, the red ink blurring as a cold sweat slicked his palms. He emptied his pockets for the tenth time, finding only a few copper coins and a crumpled receipt from a meal he could barely remember. With trembling fingers, he began dialing every single number in his old address book, ignoring the hollow ache in his chest. He waited for any voice to answer, gripping the phone so tightly that his knuckles turned a ghostly white. When the line went dead, he sank to the floor and clawed at the thinning carpet.
